banner.title: descheduler
banner.tagline: Evicts pods the scheduler placed badly or that broke their placement rules, so the scheduler can place them again.

explainer.title: Evict, then let the scheduler re-place

steps.title: Measure
steps.text: Node CPU, memory and pod counts come from metrics.k8s.io, the metrics-server API, not from the kubelet directly.
steps.scene: three node blocks with gauge needles

steps.title: Select
steps.text: LowNodeUtilization moves pods off nodes above 60 percent while others sit below 20. Failed pods and pods that broke affinity, taints or spread are also selected.
steps.scene: a funnel sorting small cubes into bins

steps.title: Filter
steps.text: DefaultEvictor skips DaemonSets, system-critical pods, and local-storage pods. PodDisruptionBudgets still apply.
steps.scene: a shield in front of protected blocks

steps.title: Evict
steps.text: The eviction goes through the API. The owning controller creates a replacement, and the scheduler picks its node.
steps.scene: a cube leaving one platform for another
